results.question: how many things can i pick up at west village, broken down by category?
results.sql:
SELECT l.category,
       COUNT(*) AS item_count
FROM nlq.listings l
JOIN nlq.meetup_spots s ON l.meetup_spot = s.name
WHERE s.name = 'West Village'
GROUP BY l.category
ORDER BY l.category;
results.answer: You can pick up 9 categories of items at West Village: bikes_transport (17), clothing (24), dorm_essentials (37), electronics (57), furniture (41), kitchen (34), other (11), sports_outdoors (22), and textbooks (53). These figures cover all time.

results.question: average weekly rent for electronics

results.question: average agreed price of completed bike sales in 2025
results.sql:

FROM nlq.deals d
JOIN nlq.listings_all l ON d.item_id = l.item_id
WHERE d.deal_type = 'sale'
  AND d.status = 'completed'
  AND l.category = 'bikes_transport'
  AND d.completed_on BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31';

results.question: which meetup spot got the most new listings in spring 2026?
results.sql:
SELECT ms.name AS meetup_spot, COUNT(*) AS new_listings
FROM nlq.listings_all la
JOIN nlq.meetup_spots ms ON la.spot_id = ms.spot_id
JOIN nlq.calendar c ON la.listed_on = c.day
WHERE c.semester = 'Spring'
  AND c.academic_year = '2025-26'
  AND la.status = 'available'
GROUP BY ms.name
ORDER BY new_listings DESC
LIMIT 1;
results.answer: The meetup spot that got the most new listings in Spring 2026 was Snell Library, with 60 listings.

results.question: what share of all listings ever posted were offered for rent?
results.sql:
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_listings,
    SUM(CASE WHEN is_for_rent THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rent_listings,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN is_for_rent THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS rent_share_percent
FROM nlq.listings_all;
results.answer: Across all time, 24.96% of the listings ever posted were offered for rent, which is 3,231 out of 12,947 total listings.

results.question: for each category, how many days on average does it take an item to sell?
results.sql:
SELECT la.category,
       ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM d.completed_at - la.listed_at) / 86400)::numeric, 2) AS avg_days_to_sell
FROM nlq.listings_all la
JOIN nlq.deals d ON d.item_id = la.item_id
WHERE la.is_for_sale = true
  AND d.deal_type = 'sale'
  AND d.status = 'completed'
  AND d.completed_at IS NOT NULL
  AND la.listed_at IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY la.category
ORDER BY la.category;
results.answer: Across all categories, the average time from listing to sale is about 11.3 days. The figures range from 11.2 days for bikes and transport to 12.1 days for other items.

results.question: what share of conversations led to a request, by meetup spot?
results.sql:
SELECT ms.name AS meetup_spot,
       COUNT(*) AS total_conversations,
       SUM(CASE WHEN cv.led_to_request THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS led_to_request_count,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN cv.led_to_request THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 2) AS share_percent
FROM nlq.conversations cv
JOIN nlq.listings_all la ON cv.item_id = la.item_id
JOIN nlq.meetup_spots ms ON la.spot_id = ms.spot_id
GROUP BY ms.name
ORDER BY ms.name;
results.answer: The share of conversations that led to a request varies by meetup spot: Curry Student Center 61.45%, Fenway (off campus) 62.91%, International Village 63.00%, Marino Recreation Center 63.61%, Mission Hill (off campus) 62.41%, Snell Library 62.30%, and West Village 63.55%. These figures cover all time.

results.question: late-return rate for rentals due during finals compared with rentals due during regular classes
results.sql:
SELECT
  c.period AS period,
  COUNT(*) AS total_rentals,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN d.returned_late THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::numeric, 2) AS late_return_rate
FROM nlq.deals d
JOIN nlq.calendar c ON d.rental_due_date = c.day
WHERE d.deal_type = 'rental'
  AND d.rental_returned_at IS NOT NULL
  AND c.period IN ('finals', 'classes')
GROUP BY c.period;
results.answer: During regular classes, there were 2,742 rentals with a late‑return rate of 20%. During finals, there were 134 rentals with a late‑return rate of 19%.

results.question: which category has the highest sell-through rate?
results.sql:
SELECT la.category,
       COUNT(*) AS total_listings,
       SUM(CASE WHEN la.status = 'sold' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sold_count,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN la.status = 'sold' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 2) AS sell_through_percent

ORDER BY sell_through_percent DESC
LIMIT 1;
